content: 1. A systematic review and meta-analysis published in The Lancet HIV in 2015 examined the global rates of hospital admissions among individuals living with HIV, providing critical insights into the burden of disease and healthcare utilization in this population. 2. Low et al. (2016) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the incidence of opportunistic infections and the impact of antiretroviral therapy (ART) among HIV-infected adults in lowand middle-income countries, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 3. Lucas et al. (1993) investigated the mortality and pathological findings associated with HIV infection in a West African city, with their findings published in AIDS. 4. Gupta et al. (2015) performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the prevalence of tuberculosis in post-mortem studies of HIV-infected adults and children in resource-limited settings, as reported in AIDS. 5. The World Health Organization's 2016 Global Tuberculosis Report provided comprehensive data on the global burden of tuberculosis, including its intersection with HIV, accessible via the WHO website. 6. Ford et al. (2016) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess tuberculosis as a cause of hospitalization and in-hospital mortality among people living with HIV worldwide, published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 7. Wiseman et al. (2011) explored the spectrum of disease and survival outcomes in HIV-infected infants with bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis, as detailed in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease. 8. Jenkins et al. (2017) performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate mortality rates in children diagnosed with tuberculosis, with their findings published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 9. The WHO's consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection (second edition) provide public health recommendations and are accessible on the WHO website. 10. Gaskell et al. (2015) reviewed the management of severe non-tuberculous bacterial infections in HIV-infected adults, as published in Expert Review of Anti-Infective Therapy. 11. Williamson et al. (2017) provided an in-depth review of cryptococcal meningitis, including its epidemiology, immunology, diagnosis, and treatment, as published in Nature Reviews Neurology. 12. Rajasingham et al. updated the global burden of HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in an analysis published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 13. Park et al. (2009) estimated the global burden of cryptococcal meningitis among individuals living with HIV/AIDS, with their findings published in AIDS. 14. Meiring et al. (2012) compared pediatric-onset and adult-onset cryptococcosis cases detected through population-based surveillance, as reported in AIDS. 15. Wang et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the prevalence and burden of Toxoplasma gondii infection in HIV-infected individuals, with findings published in The Lancet HIV. 16. Rabaud et al. (1994) conducted a French national survey on extracerebral toxoplasmosis in HIV-infected patients, with results published in Medicine (Baltimore). 17. Hernandez et al. (2017) performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the relative efficacy and safety of treatment regimens for HIV-associated cerebral toxoplasmosis, as published in HIV Medicine. 18. Ford et al. (2013) reviewed the burden of HIV-related cytomegalovirus retinitis in resource-limited settings, with findings published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 19. Manicklal et al. (2014) investigated the birth prevalence of congenital cytomegalovirus among infants born to HIV-infected women on prenatal antiretroviral prophylaxis in South Africa, as reported in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 20. Lewden et al. (2004) analyzed causes of death among HIV-infected adults in French Guiana and the French West Indies during the era of highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), as published in Médecine et Maladies Infectieuses. 21. Le et al. (2011) studied the epidemiology, seasonality, and predictors of outcomes in AIDS-associated Penicillium marneffei infections in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, as reported in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 22. Hu et al. (2013) described Penicillium marneffei infection as an emerging disease in mainland China, with findings published in Mycopathologia. 23. Le et al. presented findings from a randomized controlled trial on induction therapy for Talaromyces marneffei infection at the 2017 Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections. 24. Ford et al. (2017) discussed the evolving role of CD4 cell counts in HIV care, as published in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS. 25. Hakim et al. (2017) evaluated the impact of enhanced prophylaxis combined with antiretroviral therapy for advanced HIV infection in Africa, with findings published in The New England Journal of Medicine. 26. Mfinanga et al. (2015) conducted a randomized controlled trial on cryptococcal meningitis screening and community-based early adherence support in Tanzania and Zambia, as published in The Lancet. 27. Parkes-Ratanshi et al. (2011) assessed the efficacy of fluconazole for primary prophylaxis of cryptococcal disease in HIV-positive Ugandan adults, as reported in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 28. Bahr et al. (2013) reviewed central nervous system immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome, as published in Current Infectious Disease Reports. 29. Kimaro et al. (2017) analyzed the costs of providing antiretroviral therapy services to individuals with advanced HIV disease in Tanzania, as published in PLOS ONE. 30. Bemelmans et al. (2014) reviewed community-supported models of care for people on HIV treatment in sub-Saharan Africa, as published in Tropical Medicine & International Health. 31. Luzinda et al. presented findings on cryptococcal antigen screening using a rapid test at the point of care in rural Lesotho at the 2015 IAS Conference on HIV Pathogenesis, Treatment, and Prevention. 32. The ARROW Trial team (2013) compared routine versus clinically driven laboratory monitoring strategies for first-line antiretroviral therapy in African children with HIV, as published in The Lancet. 33. Le Roux et al. (2011) investigated bacteremia in HIV-infected children in Cape Town, South Africa, as reported in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. 34. WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience are accessible on the WHO website. 35. WHO guidelines on the public health response to pretreatment HIV drug resistance were published in 2017. 36. WHO vaccine position papers, including the position on the measles vaccine, are available on the WHO website and in the Weekly Epidemiological Record. 37. Dutertrè et al. analyzed the risk of IRIS requiring hospitalization following the initiation of antiretroviral therapy containing integrase inhibitors, as published in JAIDS. 38. Kitson et al. presented findings from the REALITY trial on raltegravir-intensified quadruple therapy versus triple first-line ART at the 2016 International AIDS Conference. 39. Fox and Goemaere (2006) described the patient selection process for antiretroviral treatment in Khayelitsha, South Africa, as published in the Cambridge Quarterly of Healthcare Ethics. 40. Rosen and Fox (2011) conducted a systematic review on retention in HIV care between testing and treatment in sub-Saharan Africa, as published in PLOS Medicine.
